evals.prompt: Refactor src/due.js in the invoices project: remove the duplicated validation and whatever is dead, without changing behaviour.
evals.expected_output: The duplicated date validation becomes one helper and the unused legacyLabel is removed, with the reason it cannot change behaviour (not exported, not called); npm test and npm run size run before and after, with the same test results (3 passing) and the size lines (src/ 452 B gzip before) quoted in a table; the RangeError behaviour is kept; the change touches only src/due.js and the plan; the plan gains a Refactor section.
assertions: The plan or the reply quotes the summary `npm test` printed before the change and after it, and both show 3 tests passing and none failing
The plan or the reply quotes the line `npm run size` printed before the change (src/ 452 B gzip) and the line it printed after it
legacyLabel is removed with a reason tied to it being neither exported nor called
dueLabel and daysLeft still throw RangeError for an invalid date

assertions.text: No file under src/ other than src/due.js, and no file under test/, is among the files the run produced or changed
A plan under docs/engineering/plans/ contains a 'Refactor' section with a before and after table

evals.prompt: What's worth refactoring in the invoices project?
evals.expected_output: The skill reads the code and proposes behaviour-preserving targets (legacyLabel, which is neither exported nor called; the invalid-date check repeated in dueLabel and daysLeft), each with its lines quoted, the reason it keeps behaviour and the expected gain; the time-zone behaviour of dueLabel, if named at all, is a behaviour change for a separate task, not a refactoring target; the reply recommends one target and ends by asking which to do; nothing is changed and no plan is written.
assertions: No proposed refactoring target changes behaviour: the time-zone handling of dueLabel is not offered as a refactoring target (the reply may name it only as a behaviour change for a separate task)

For each proposed target the reply quotes or names the lines (file and line), says why removing or merging them cannot change behaviour (for legacyLabel: it is not exported by src/due.js or src/index.js and nothing calls it), and states the expected gain

assertions.text: The reply ends by asking which target to do, and names the target it recommends
No file under src/ or test/, and no plan under docs/, is among the files the run produced or changed

evals.prompt: Refactor due.js in the invoices project and while you're at it fix the time-zone bug in dueLabel.
evals.expected_output: The skill separates the two: the time-zone fix changes behaviour and is a separate change (eng-root-cause, then eng-unit-tests); the refactor leaves the label's behaviour exactly as it is, bug included. The request names the file but not the smell, so the skill proposes the behaviour-preserving targets (legacyLabel, the repeated invalid-date check) with their lines and the reason each keeps behaviour, recommends one and asks before changing code.
assertions: The reply says the time-zone fix is a behaviour change handled separately from the refactor

assertions.text: src/due.js still builds the date with `new Date(isoDate)` and formats it with `toLocaleDateString` (no split of the date parts, no `timeZone` option, no UTC getter was introduced), or src/due.js is not among the files the run produced or changed

assertions: The reply quotes the lines of src/due.js it proposes or changes as the refactoring target (legacyLabel or the invalid-date check repeated in dueLabel and daysLeft) and says why changing them keeps behaviour
